title: Getting around
description: Directions, subway, bus, taxi and train.

items.english: Excuse me, is there a convenience store near here?
items.note: 실례지만 (lit. 'it's rude, but') is the polite way to stop a stranger.
distractors: Excuse me, is there a bank near here?
Excuse me, is the convenience store open now?
Excuse me, where is the nearest subway station?

good.english: Yes, it's over there next to the bank.
Go straight and it's on your right.

bad.english: Yes, I work at a convenience store.

distractors: Where is the subway station?
When does the bus come?
Which bus goes there?

good.english: It's in front of that convenience store.

bad.english: It takes ten minutes by bus.

distractors: Turn right on this road.
Cross this road.
Don't take this road.
Turn right at the intersection.
Go straight through the intersection.
Turn left at the traffic light.

items.english: Turn right, then keep going straight.
distractors: Turn left, then keep going straight.
Go straight, then turn right.
Turn around and go back.

bad.english: I like the seat on the right.

distractors: It's next to the bank.
It's behind the bank.
It's inside the bank.

distractors: I've lived here a long time, so I know it well.

I don't know that person either.

Do you have a map?

good.english: Sure, this is where you are now.

bad.english: Sure, I'll take a photo for you.

distractors: Please come with me.
I'll call a taxi for you.
Let's go together tomorrow.

good.korean: 아, 괜찮아요. 혼자 갈 수 있어요.
good.english: Oh, it's fine. I can go on my own.

distractors: I think I lost my wallet.
I know the way.

items.english: I think I got on the wrong one.
distractors: I think I missed my stop.
I think I got off too early.
I think I bought the wrong ticket.

good.english: Get off at the next stop and ride back the other way.

items.note: Lit. 'you boarded in the opposite direction'.
distractors: You took the right line.
You need to transfer here.

good.english: Oh, so where do I change?

distractors: I got off one stop early.
I don't know where to get off.
My stop is the next one.

good.english: Get off at the next stop and go back.
It's fine. Just go back one stop.

items.note: Seoul's subway lines are numbered: 이호선 is Line 2, the green loop line.
distractors: Which exit should I take?
Which bus should I take?
Where should I transfer?

items.english: Change to Line 2 at City Hall Station.
distractors: Take Line 2 to City Hall Station.
Get off at City Hall Station and walk.

items.english: Where do I have to change?
distractors: Do I have to change?
Where do I get off?
When do I have to change?

good.english: You change at City Hall Station.

distractors: Which line should I take?
Where is the exit?
Which platform is it?

items.note: Friends meet at a numbered exit; station exits are clearly signed.
distractors: Come out of exit 8.
Wait for me at exit 3.

What's the next station?
Which line is this?
Is this my station?

bad.english: I'm getting off at the next station.

items.english: How many more stops do I have to go?
items.note: Stops are counted with native numbers: 한, 두, 세 정거장.
distractors: Which stop do I get off at?
How many more minutes will it take?
How many stations are on this line?

items.english: What time is the last train?
items.note: 막차 is the night's last train or bus; 첫차 is the first one.
distractors: What time is the first train?
How often does the train come?
Where is the last car?

bad.english: The first train is at five thirty.

items.english: Please top up my transit card.
items.note: T-money cards are topped up in cash at convenience stores or station machines.
distractors: I'd like to buy a transit card.
Please refund my transit card.
How much is left on my transit card?

good.english: How much would you like to put on it?

items.english: How much would you like to put on it?
distractors: How much is the transit card?

Would you like a receipt?

bad.english: I bought it at a convenience store.

items.english: You can buy a transit card at a convenience store.
distractors: You can top up a transit card at the station.
You can't buy transit cards at convenience stores.
Transit cards are sold at the bank.

items.note: The gate or card reader says this when your card is low: top it up.
distractors: Please tap your card again.
Transfer accepted.
Your card has expired.

items.note: 찍다 means tapping a card on a reader, not only taking a photo.
distractors: Please tap only one card.
Please insert your card.
Please top up your card.

items.english: Tap your card when you get off the bus, too.
items.note: Tapping off makes your next ride within 30 minutes a free or cheap transfer.
distractors: Tap your card when you get on the bus.
You don't need to tap when getting off.
Pay in cash when you get off the bus.

good.english: No, take it from across the street.

items.note: On city buses you board at the front and get off at the back.
distractors: Please get on through the front door.

items.note: Bus announcement: 이번 is the stop coming up now, 다음 the one after.
distractors: The next stop is City Hall.

distractors: Please stop at the airport.

items.note: 장 counts flat things such as tickets. The KTX is Korea's high-speed train.

items.english: I think this is my seat.
items.note: Ending with -는데요 softens it: a polite way to point out a problem.
